description.short_caption: Swollen foot with erythema, suggestive of inflammation or infection.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a foot with notable swelling and diffuse erythema, particularly over the dorsum. The skin appears taut, and there is no visible ulceration or drainage. The findings are consistent with an inflammatory or infectious process, such as cellulitis. The image is well-lit and focuses on the affected area, providing clear visualization of the changes.

description.short_caption: Erythematous discoloration of the palm, suggestive of a systemic or localized condition.
description.detailed_description: The image shows the palm of a hand with diffuse erythema, particularly prominent in the central and distal areas. The skin appears smooth without visible scaling, ulceration, or vesicles. The fingers and thumb are extended, and the erythema does not appear to involve the dorsal aspect of the hand. The lighting is even, and the image is clear, allowing for detailed examination of the skin changes.

description.short_caption: Swollen hand with erythema and skin changes.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a dorsal view of a hand with significant swelling, erythema, and a shiny appearance of the skin. The skin appears taut, with some areas of scaling or dryness visible. No visible wounds, ulcerations, or purulent drainage are present. The findings suggest an inflammatory or infectious process involving the soft tissues of the hand.

description.short_caption: Erythematous rash with linear markings on the sole of the foot.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the sole of a foot with a diffuse erythematous rash. There are linear, slightly raised markings visible, suggestive of a serpiginous pattern. The surrounding skin appears intact without ulceration or desquamation. The image is well-lit, and the findings are clearly visible.

description.short_caption: Erythematous and scaly lesions on both knees.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the anterior aspect of both knees. The skin exhibits erythema, scaling, and thickened plaques, particularly over the patellar regions. The lesions appear symmetrical and are associated with mild hyperpigmentation. No visible ulceration or discharge is noted. The surrounding skin shows mild discoloration but no overt signs of infection.
